text.p: Australasian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd is expected to post a moderate pickup when it reports first half profits on Friday, but analysts believe better earnings will be achieved in the final six months of 1996/97.
First half net profit before abnormals to December 31, 1996 is seen ranging between A$55 million and A$59 million, from A$52.9 million in the same period in 1995.
Analysts said most of the improvement is seen coming from write-downs and improved financial management rather than underlying earnings growth.
Goodman Fielder has become more upbeat about its performance in recent times, predicting full year double digit growth in pre-abnormal profit at its annual general meeting last November.
Managing director David Hearn said the first half would be relatively flat, with a much stronger second half as the impact of lower wheat prices began to flow through to the bottom line.
The food group has also been continuing its efforts under Hearn to streamline its business and benefit from its size.
New Zealand operations were revamped in January, the Steggles poultry business was restructured in February, and the trading assets of a small European starch business were sold in December.
For the full year, the market expects a net profit before abnormals in the range A$112 million to A$120 million, with most analysts forecasting a result around A$116-A$118 million.
This would compare with a pre-abnormals net-profit of A$100.7 million in 1995/96.
"The first half will be impacted by the high wheat costs, which should be coming off in the second half, so that's really what will hold them back," said a third Sydney-based analyst.
Analysts said the market will look for Goodman to renew predictions of solid double digit profit growth on Friday confirming its improvement over the full year.
Goodman Fielder shares closed unchanged at A$1.58 on Wednesday.
